meta.title: Multi-Key Rotation
meta.description: Give a MiniMax Token Plan route several named API keys and let the plugin rotate between them automatically. This release supports MiniMax Token Plan only (the minimax and minimax-cn routes): it is the one subscription whose quota is published as two windows — a 5-hour one and a weekly one — and the one whose spent-plan error the adapter misclassifies. The pool takes the route over as soon as it loads: it writes one of its keys into the provider’s own credential reference, so requests authenticate with a pool key instead of the key stored in Settings → Models. When a request fails with a plan quota, a quota, a rate limit, or an auth error, the plugin writes the next key of the pool into the provider's credential reference and retries the request — no restart, no lost context. Open the plugin's tab in the Plugins settings section (Settings → Plugins → Multi-Key Rotation) to configure it: add the keys one at a time or paste several at once, choose the failures that trigger a switch, pick between switching only on a failure and switching also before every request, and save. When the pool is searched for the next key, the key whose weekly window resets soonest comes first, and among those the one whose 5-hour window resets soonest — a key that is about to reset is spent before it expires. Each key's remaining quota is shown for both windows, the 5-hour one and the weekly one, next to each reset time. A compact capsule beside the model selector in the composer shows the key that is in use, its two remaining shares, and the countdown to each window's reset. Key values are stored in the Harness credential store and are never written to the profile configuration. Turning the plugin off stops the rotation and leaves the provider on whichever key was written last.
